narrator: A warm, gentle American woman in her late sixties telling the true story of her own life, like a beloved audiobook narrator. Soft Pennsylvania accent, calm and intimate, a little husky with age, quietly emotional, never theatrical. Sounds like a grandmother talking to a friend late at night.

I was twenty-four in the summer of 1952, and I believed three things with absolute certainty. A good book could rescue almost any bad afternoon. My mother would never approve of the man I loved. And Daniel Mercer would marry me before the first snow. When I lifted the photograph, an envelope slid onto the table. It was yellowed and thin, with my maiden name written across the front in Daniel's unmistakable hand. I stood so still I could hear the rain striking the porch rail. Then I opened it.
charles: A frail, wealthy American man in his mid seventies, a retired small-town banker. Refined, once commanding voice now weak, breathy and trembling with guilt and fear. Old-fashioned East Coast polish.
